name: France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship
region: National — Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
application_deadline: Expected early January 2027, set by Campus France for institutions (last round: 8 January 2026). The French institution's internal deadline is earlier.
call_notes: As of 24 September 2026 the Campus France page still shows the 2026 session; the last call opened on 1 October 2025, so expect the 2027 call in early October 2026. Only French institutions submit applications, so students must be in touch with their target programme now.
benefits: Return economy airfare, domestic travel to the study city, health insurance, help with housing, cultural activities. Tuition is waived only for national diplomas at public institutions; otherwise not covered.

sections.title: Important dates
sections.body:
Last completed round (2026 session):
Call opened: 1 October 2025
Deadline for Campus France to receive applications: 8 January 2026 (included)
Results published from: 30 March 2026

Next round (2027 session): not yet published as of 24 September 2026.
Expect the same shape: opening in early October 2026, closing in early January 2027, results from late March 2027.
Studies must start between 1 September and 30 November 2027. The start date cannot be postponed.

Each French institution sets its own internal deadline for Eiffel nominations, usually weeks before the Campus France deadline. NOTE — verify the internal deadline with the programme itself.

sections.title: Who can apply
sections.body:
The student does not apply. Only applications submitted by a French higher education institution are accepted. Applications sent by students or by foreign institutions are declared ineligible.

Age limits: up to 29 years old at master's level, up to 35 years old at PhD level. NOTE — verify how age is counted (reference date) in the 2027 rules.
For foreign (non-French) students. NOTE — verify the rule on dual nationals holding French nationality in the 2027 rules.

Eligible programmes: a master's-level degree accredited by the French state, a nationally accredited engineering degree (diplôme d'ingénieur), or a PhD under joint supervision (cotutelle or co-direction) with a partner institution abroad.

Seven priority fields:
Science and technology: biology and health; ecological transition; mathematics and digital sciences; engineering.
Humanities and social sciences: French history, language and civilisation; law and political science; economics and management.

Eiffel cannot be combined with another French government scholarship, an Erasmus+ scholarship or an AUF scholarship. A student holding two must give one up.

sections.title: What it pays
sections.body:
Monthly living allowance (from January 2026):
Master: €1,200 per month.
PhD: €2,000 per month.
NOTE — verify the PhD figure: the French 2026 rules on campusfrance.org and the Campus France recipients' page say €2,000, but an English copy of the 2026 rules and one Campus France page say €2,100.

Duration (master): up to 12 months for M2 entry, up to 24 months for M1 entry, up to 36 months for an engineering programme.
Duration (PhD): 12, 18 or 36 months from 1 September. 36 months is only for new students starting year one who are not already studying in France.
One extra month from August is possible for a language course, if it is written into the application. The course fee itself is not covered.

Also covered: economy return airfare (reimbursed on receipts, capped by a ministry rate), train or bus from the arrival airport to the study city, temporary health insurance then free top-up insurance, choice of CROUS or private housing, cultural outings.

Tuition: waived only for a national diploma (master, doctorate) or accredited engineering degree at a public institution under the Higher Education ministry. Everywhere else, tuition and programme fees are not paid by Eiffel. Business schools and private institutions will charge full fees.

The first payment is sent by Western Union; after that, payments go to a French bank account. The allowance starts only once the student has arrived and started the programme.

sections.title: How to apply
sections.body:
1. Shortlist master's or PhD programmes in France in one of the seven priority fields.
2. Apply for admission to those programmes (through Études en France or the institution directly, as the programme requires). Do this by early autumn.
3. Email the programme director or international office and ask whether they will nominate the student for Eiffel, and by what internal date.
4. Supply the institution with everything it asks for by its internal deadline. The institution builds and submits the file to Campus France.
5. Wait for results from late March. Campus France publishes them; the institution informs the student.
6. If selected, complete Études en France and the visa (see For Pakistani students). Studies start between 1 September and 30 November.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.body:
The institution decides the exact list. Typically:
Passport.
Degree certificates and full transcripts (HEC-attested for Pakistani degrees).
CV.
Statement of purpose / study project, clearly tied to the student's career plan.
Recommendation letters.
English test (IELTS or equivalent) for English-taught programmes; French-level proof (DELF/DALF or TCF) for French-taught ones.
For PhD: research proposal and evidence of the cotutelle or co-direction arrangement.
NOTE — verify the institution's own list; it varies.

sections.title: For Pakistani students
sections.body:
Campus France Pakistan runs the Études en France (EeF) procedure, with interviews at Alliance Française in Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad. The EeF certificate is needed before booking a visa appointment.

Attestation Campus France Pakistan asks for:
SSC/O-level and HSSC/A-level documents attested by IBCC.
Bachelor's/master's degree and transcript attested by HEC.
Passport valid until 18 months after the visa appointment.
IELTS or other English proof, CV with experience letters, gap explanation letter if any, and the final acceptance letter.

EeF fee: PKR 30,000 paid to Alliance Française Karachi (NOTE — verify the current fee). French government scholarship holders such as Eiffel recipients have the EeF fee waived on uploading proof.
After file validation there is an academic interview at the nearest Alliance Française, with original documents.

Visa: appointment through AEG (frenchvisa.aeg.com.pk), interview at the French consulate in Islamabad. A decision takes between 2 weeks and 2 months, so start as soon as results are out in late March.
PhD fellowship holders apply for a Talent Passport visa instead, and EeF is not required.

Campus France Pakistan also advertises a separate France Excellence Pakistan call (climate change). NOTE — verify whether it runs for 2027.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Telling a student to apply to Campus France directly. The application is ineligible unless an institution submits it.
Starting in December. By then most institutions have closed their internal Eiffel selection.
Choosing a field outside the seven priority fields, or a private degree not accredited by the French state.
Promising free tuition. It is only waived at public institutions for national diplomas.
Ignoring the age cap (29 master, 35 PhD).
Holding Eiffel alongside Erasmus+ or another French government award. One must be declined.
Leaving HEC and IBCC attestation until after results, which delays EeF and the visa.
Assuming a deferral is possible. The start date cannot be postponed.

name: DAAD Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)
region: National — German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD), funded by the BMZ
application_deadline: Set by each course, not by DAAD. Most 2027/28 course deadlines fall between August and October 2026 (e.g. Freiburg MEG: 15 October 2026).
call_notes: The 2027/2028 course list is out (DAAD, June 2026) and course windows are open now; several close in October 2026. Apply to the course itself, never to DAAD.
benefits: Health, accident and personal liability insurance; travel allowance; possible rent subsidy and family allowance; study fees usually waived by the course.

sections.title: How EPOS works
sections.body:
EPOS is a fixed list of development-related master's courses at German universities. DAAD funds scholarships only on these courses.

The student applies to the course, not to DAAD. The course's selection committee picks candidates and recommends them; only then are they asked to upload to the DAAD portal, and DAAD makes the final decision.

A student may apply to at most 3 EPOS courses, listed in order of priority, with one motivation letter covering all of them.

The 2027/2028 list has about 25 courses, all master's level (MSc, MA, MBA, MEng), in economics, development cooperation, engineering, urban planning, agriculture and forestry, environmental sciences, public health and education.

sections.title: Important dates
sections.body:
There is no single EPOS deadline. The official 2027/2028 list (DAAD, June 2026) says "see website of the course" for every course.

Example, confirmed on the course page: Environmental Governance (MEG), University of Freiburg, applications 15 June to 15 October 2026 for study starting October 2027.

Most courses close between August and October 2026. Check each course the student wants separately, well before its date.

Development Management (RU Bochum) takes students only every two years; its next intake is 2028.

Studies begin in autumn 2027 (German-taught courses start earlier with a German course). NOTE — verify when DAAD sends final decisions; it is not published in the database entry.

sections.title: Who can apply
sections.body:
Graduates from countries on the OECD DAC list of developing countries. Pakistan is on that list.

A Bachelor's degree, normally a four-year degree, with an above-average result (roughly the top third).

At least two years of professional experience after the Bachelor's, at the time of application. Freiburg MEG states that internships and volunteer work do not count, and academic employment generally does not.

Degrees should normally be no more than six years old.

Not resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the application deadline.

The applicant must also meet the course's own admission rules.

sections.title: What it pays
sections.body:
Master's: €992 per month.
Duration: 12 to 42 months depending on the course (including any German course).

Also: health, accident and personal liability insurance, and a travel allowance (unless travel is paid by the home country or another source). A monthly rent subsidy and family allowance may be paid in some cases.

The DAAD entry also gives a doctoral rate (€1,300, €1,400 from February 2026), but the 2027/2028 course list contains master's courses only.

Freiburg MEG says EPOS holders are exempt from its study fees. NOTE — verify fee waivers course by course.

sections.title: How to apply
sections.body:
1. Open the 2027/2028 EPOS course list and pick up to 3 courses that match the student's degree and job.
2. Open each course's own website and note its deadline, submission method and extra requirements.
3. Get the EPOS application form and checklist from the DAAD database entry or the course page.
4. Prepare the documents below. Everything must be in English or German.
5. Submit to each course directly, by the course's method (Freiburg MEG, for example, wants one merged PDF by email).
6. If the course recommends the student, they receive an invitation to upload to the DAAD portal.
7. Wait for DAAD's final decision, then start visa preparation at once.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.body:
EPOS application form and completed checklist.
CV on the Europass template, in reverse chronological order.
One motivation letter explaining the course choices and their link to development work at home.
Recommendation letter from the current employer: dated, on letterhead, signed and stamped.
Employment certificates proving at least two years of relevant work.
Language certificates.
Certified copies of degrees and transcripts.
Any extra items the course asks for, such as academic references.

Incomplete applications are rejected.

sections.title: For Pakistani students
sections.body:
Work experience: the two-year rule is enforced. A fresh graduate is not eligible, however strong.

Degree length: a two-year BA/BSc is unlikely to meet the four-year Bachelor's expectation. Check the course's rules before applying.

Language: English-taught courses set their own IELTS/TOEFL scores. German-taught courses (e.g. Textile Machinery, TU Dresden) need certified German at B1 when applying and DSH 2 or TestDaF 4 before studies; DAAD includes a 6-month German course.

HEC attestation: NOTE — verify whether the course and the German mission want HEC-attested degrees and transcripts; get them attested early either way.

APS: the DAAD entry asks only applicants from China for an APS certificate. uni-assist lists APS offices only in China, Vietnam and India, and the German Embassy's Pakistan student-visa page does not mention APS. Several Pakistani agent websites say APS is mandatory; those claims do not match the official pages. NOTE — verify with the German Embassy Islamabad before telling a student APS is not needed.

Visa: book through the Federal Foreign Office Consular Services Portal. Sindh and Balochistan residents apply at the Consulate General Karachi; Islamabad, Punjab, KP, GB and AJK at the Embassy Islamabad. The mission reports a high volume of student visas. NOTE — verify current waiting times and whether the DAAD award letter replaces the blocked account.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Writing to DAAD instead of applying to the course.
Applying to more than 3 courses, or sending a different motivation letter to each.
Counting internships or volunteer work towards the two years.
An employer letter without date, signature or stamp.
Using a free-form CV instead of Europass.
Missing a course deadline by assuming all EPOS courses close on the same date.
Applying to Development Management (Bochum) for 2027; its next intake is 2028.

name: Stipendium Hungaricum
application_deadline: Expected mid-January 2027 (last round: 15 January 2026, 14:00 CET on the Hungarian portal; HEC portal closed the same day at 16:00 PKT)
call_notes: The 2027/2028 call is not out yet. Last year the Call PDF was posted in October 2025 and the application system opened on 14 November 2025; HEC posts its own advertisement with the Pakistan quota around the same time.
stipend_amount: HUF 43,700/month (bachelor, master, one-tier master, non-degree) · HUF 140,000 then 180,000/month (PhD)
benefits: Tuition exemption, free dormitory place or HUF 40,000/month towards rent, Hungarian health cover plus up to HUF 65,000/year supplementary insurance. Paid 12 months a year. HEC also reimburses air tickets up to Rs 200,000 each way.

sections.title: Important dates
sections.body:
Last completed round (2026/2027):
Call for Applications published: October 2025
Application system opened: 14 November 2025
Deadline, Hungarian portal: 15 January 2026, 14:00 CET
Deadline, HEC portal: 15 January 2026, 16:00 PKT (12:00 CET, two hours before the Hungarian one)
HAT/USAT test for late takers: 1 February 2026 (registration opened around 8 December 2025)
HEC nomination list sent to Hungary: by 28 February 2026
University entrance exams and interviews: mid-March to end of May 2026
Results from Tempus: end of June to mid-July 2026
Missing documents and acceptance in the system: by 1 August 2026
Arrival in Hungary: by 30 September 2026

Next round (2027/2028): not announced yet. Expect the Call in October 2026, the system to open mid-November 2026 and both deadlines around 15 January 2027. Confirm every date against the new Call and the HEC advertisement before quoting it.

sections.title: Who can apply
sections.body:
Pakistani or AJ&K citizens only, applying through HEC as the Sending Partner. HEC excludes dual nationals.
Must be 18 by 31 August of the start year (last round: born on or before 31 August 2008). No upper age limit.
Bachelor and one-tier master (Medicine, Dentistry, Pharmacy, DVM and similar): HSSC/Intermediate or equivalent, completed by 1 August of the start year.
Master: a 16-year bachelor's degree, completed by 1 August.
PhD: MS/MPhil or equivalent (17/18 years), completed by 1 August. PhD has its own separate Call.
Result-awaiting and final-year students may apply, with the final documents uploaded by 1 August.
HEC requires HAT or USAT at 50% or more. HAT is valid 2 years, USAT 1 year. NTS GAT and GRE are not accepted.
Students already holding a scholarship from their university or institution are not eligible (HEC FAQ).
Only fields offered by both HEC and Hungary for Pakistan; HEC publishes the list of eligible study fields.

sections.title: What it pays
sections.body:
Tuition: fully exempt.
Stipend: HUF 43,700/month (about EUR 110) for bachelor, master, one-tier master and non-degree, for 12 months a year.
PhD: HUF 140,000/month (about EUR 355) for the first four semesters, HUF 180,000/month (about EUR 460) for the second four.
Housing: a free dormitory place where capacity allows, otherwise HUF 40,000/month (about EUR 100) towards rent.
Health: Hungarian state health care plus supplementary insurance up to HUF 65,000 (about EUR 165) a year.
HEC: reimburses the air ticket out and back after completion, up to Rs 200,000 each way.

The Call itself says this is only a contribution and students must add their own money. In Budapest HUF 40,000 will not cover a private room.
Students who skip the compulsory Hungarian as a foreign language course lose the stipend; those who fail its exam have it cut to HUF 30,000.
Euro figures use the Call's 13 October 2025 exchange rate; amounts are for the 2026/2027 round.

sections.title: How to apply
sections.body:
1. Choose up to two programmes, in order of preference. The programmes, their order and the study mode cannot be changed after the deadline.
2. Check each programme's entry and language requirements by opening it in apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu.
3. Book HAT or USAT early if the student has no valid score of 50% or more.
4. Create or use the HEC common profile (CNIC as user ID) and apply on scholarship.hec.gov.pk. Fill every field.
5. Register on apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu, upload the documents and press Submit. A saved but unsubmitted application is rejected.
6. Submit the HEC application before 16:00 PKT on the deadline day, which is earlier than the Hungarian cut-off.
7. HEC shortlists and may hold its own test or interview, then nominates by end of February.
8. Nominated candidates sit the university entrance exam or interview (March to May). 56 out of 100 is the minimum.
9. If awarded: accept in the system and upload missing documents by 1 August, then apply for the Hungarian visa (July to August).
10. Before departure: HEC degree and IBCC attestation, the medical certificate on the official template, and the HEC bond.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.body:
Online application form in English with a photo taken within the last 2 years.
Motivation letter: at least one page, Times New Roman 12, in the language of the programme.
Proof of English at the level the university sets. Where the previous degree was taught in English, proof of that can be uploaded instead.
School certificate (bachelor) or degree certificate (master) plus transcripts for all years, with translations where not in English.
Passport data page. Without a passport, upload the CNIC data page and a signed declaration, and add the passport by 1 August.
Statement for Application and Privacy Notice: accepted by clicking in the system, not uploaded.
PhD only: research plan (at least 2 pages), recommendation letter, and a supervisor statement if the doctoral school asks for it (last round by 15 March).
Arts and music: portfolio as the programme specifies.
Each file must be 4 MB or smaller.

Medical certificate: not uploaded. Only awardees need it, on the official template, issued no earlier than 1 November of the application year, and it is carried to Hungary for the compulsory medical check.

sections.title: For Pakistani students
sections.body:
Two portals, both mandatory: scholarship.hec.gov.pk and apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu. Missing either one kills the application.
HEC allocation for 2026/2027: 200 bachelor, 70 one-tier master (20 Medicine, 10 Dentistry, 40 other), 100 master and 30 PhD places. Check the new HEC advertisement for 2027/2028 figures.
HAT/USAT at 50% is compulsory for every level, including bachelor.
Attestation is not needed at the application stage. After nomination, degrees and transcripts must be attested by HEC, and school certificates by IBCC. O and A level students need IBCC equivalence.
Awardees sign a bond with HEC on legal paper: no change of discipline, and return to serve Pakistan after the degree, with a penalty recoverable from the student or guarantor.
Medicine and Dentistry: only at Hungarian universities listed by PMDC, and the student must follow PMDC's rules for foreign admissions.
Engineering: HEC's FAQ says PEC recognises the undergraduate engineering programmes of the University of Debrecen and BME; others are at the student's own risk.
Government employees must apply through proper channel.
Passport, medical and police certificates are needed after HEC's provisional selection.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Applying on only one portal.
Working to the 14:00 CET Hungarian deadline and missing HEC's 16:00 PKT cut-off, which falls two hours earlier.
Saving the Hungarian application without pressing Submit.
No valid HAT/USAT score, or one below 50%.
Putting Medicine as second choice: the Call says medical places are usually filled from first-choice applicants.
Picking the partial (exchange) version of a programme by mistake. Most programmes appear twice and the study mode cannot be changed later.
Choosing a Hungarian-language preparatory year expecting to study in English afterwards. That route only leads to a Hungarian-taught degree.
Using a Hotmail or Yahoo address, or a university email that will expire. Tempus mail lands in spam.
Treating the stipend as enough to live on.
Registering more than one account or applying through more than one Sending Partner, which is an automatic rejection.

The Call states the application is free and advises against applying through agencies. The student must hold and submit their own accounts; our role is advice and document checks.

name: Romanian Government Scholarships (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
application_deadline: Expected end of March 2027 (last round: 16 February to 31 March 2026)
call_notes: The 2027/2028 round is not announced. Last year's window was 16 February to 31 March 2026 with results around 15 July 2026; applications go only through the Study in Romania scholarships platform, never the embassy.
benefits: No tuition or registration fees, a monthly stipend, dormitory accommodation where places are available, and a free one-year Romanian language preparatory year. Air fare is not covered.

sections.title: Important dates
sections.body:
Last completed round (2026/2027):
Applications opened: 16 February 2026
Deadline: 31 March 2026
Results announced: around 15 July 2026
After selection: visa and enrolment formalities before the academic year starts.

Next round (2027/2028): not announced yet. Expect the platform to open around mid-February 2027 and close around the end of March 2027. Confirm the dates on the platform before quoting them.
There is no HEC nomination step for this scheme; the student applies directly.

sections.title: Who can apply
sections.body:
Citizens of non-EU countries, so Pakistani citizens qualify.
An average across the years of the last completed qualification of at least 7 out of 10 in the Romanian system, or a Good grade. NOTE — verify how the committee converts Pakistani marks or CGPA to this scale; no official conversion is published.
Bachelor: for holders of a school-leaving certificate (HSSC, A levels or equivalent). Programmes run 3 to 6 years.
Master: for bachelor graduates. Programmes run 1, 1.5 or 2 years.
PhD: 4 years. The candidate must have the written agreement of a doctoral supervisor at the chosen doctoral school before applying, and pass the admission interview.
Not eligible: people of Romanian origin or from Romanian historical communities, anyone who requested or holds protection in Romania, stateless persons, diplomatic and international-organisation staff in Romania and their families, and current Romanian state scholarship holders at the same study level.
No age limit is stated on the official page. Under-18s at course start need notarised parental consent.
All fields except Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy.

sections.title: Language of study
sections.body:
Bachelor and master are funded only for programmes taught in Romanian.
Students who do not speak Romanian first take a one-year Romanian preparatory year, so a 3-year degree becomes a 4-year commitment.
Exempt from the preparatory year: those with at least three consecutive years of study in Romanian, those who pass the Romanian language test, and PhD holders who choose a programme in a foreign language.
PhD candidates may choose Romanian or a foreign language set by the doctoral school.
Tell a student who wants an English-taught bachelor or master that this scheme does not fund one.

sections.title: What it pays
sections.body:
No tuition or registration fees.
Monthly stipend: €65 bachelor, €75 master, €85 PhD. These are the rates set under Government Decision 844/2008, as confirmed in a Romanian state university's 2024/2025 senate decision; the MFA page itself gives no figure. NOTE — verify they still apply for 2027/2028.
NOTE — verify the preparatory-year rate. The official page says a monthly stipend is paid in that year but gives no amount.
NOTE — verify whether it is paid in lei at the euro equivalent and whether bachelor and master stipends stop over the summer; older MFA notices said they did and PhD stipends did not.
Dormitory accommodation within the allocated subsidy, only as far as places are available.
Not covered: international travel, visa costs, and living costs beyond the stipend.

The stipend is very small. A student must plan their own funds for food and living costs.

sections.title: How to apply
sections.body:
1. Pick the university and programme (Romanian-taught for bachelor or master). PhD candidates secure a supervisor's written agreement first.
2. Get every study document attested and apostilled in Pakistan (see For Pakistani students).
3. Have authorised translations into English, French, Spanish or Romanian made where needed.
4. Scan each document separately from the original, as PDF.
5. Create an account on https://scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro/ (also reachable via Apply for MFA scholarships on studyinromania.gov.ro) and complete the application.
6. Upload the documents, sign the GDPR declaration and submit before the deadline (31 March last round).
7. The MFA and the Ministry of Education select by file competition. Watch for results around mid-July.
8. If selected: apply for the Romanian student visa and arrange travel.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.body:
Diploma for the last completed level (HSSC for bachelor; bachelor's degree for master; master's degree for PhD), with authorised translation if needed.
Transcripts for the same levels, with translation if needed.
Birth certificate, with translation if needed.
First three pages of a valid passport.
CV in English, French or Romanian.
Signed GDPR declaration.
PhD: letter of intent with list of publications, detailed research project, and the supervisor's agreement.
If applicable: proof of name change; certificate of passing the final exam where the diploma is not yet issued; Romanian preparatory year or language certificate; notarised parental consent for under-18s.
All study documents must be apostilled under the Hague Convention or authenticated by the home authorities.

sections.title: For Pakistani students
sections.body:
No HEC involvement: the student applies directly on the Romanian platform. No Pakistan quota is published.
Pakistan joined the Apostille Convention in March 2023, so the MOFA apostille is the route for Pakistani documents.
Order of work: HEC attestation for degrees and transcripts, IBCC attestation for matric and intermediate (and IBCC equivalence for O and A levels), then MOFA apostille. NOTE — verify MOFA's current prerequisite list on apostille.mofa.gov.pk before booking.
Birth certificate: NOTE — verify with MOFA which birth certificate (NADRA computerised or union council) it will apostille and what prior verification it needs.
The Romanian Embassy in Islamabad republishes the call but does not take applications. Applications sent to embassies, ministries or by email are rejected.
Students aiming at MBBS, BDS or Pharm-D must look elsewhere: those fields are excluded.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Sending the file to the embassy or by email instead of the platform.
Uploading unapostilled documents, or one combined PDF instead of one scan per document.
Applying for an English-taught bachelor or master; only Romanian-taught programmes are funded at those levels.
Applying for Medicine, Dentistry or Pharmacy.
A PhD application without the supervisor's written agreement.
Leaving attestation and apostille until March. HEC, IBCC and MOFA each take time.
After award: changing field, poor attendance or missing the required credits loses the scholarship, and it cannot be reinstated.

name: MAEC-AECID Scholarships (Spanish Government)
region: National — Agencia Española de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo (AECID)
call_notes: Pakistani citizens were not eligible for any MAEC-AECID master's call in 2024-25, 2025-26 or 2026-27. Do not advise students to plan around this scholarship unless a new BOE call names Pakistan.
stipend_amount: EUR 2,000/month in the 2026-27 África-Med Máster call (not open to Pakistan)
benefits: Monthly allowance and health insurance in Spain for the award period. Each programme's call sets its own amount, countries and conditions.

sections.title: Pakistan is not eligible
sections.body:
Short answer for counsellors: Pakistani citizens cannot currently apply for a MAEC-AECID master's scholarship.

MAEC-AECID is not one scholarship. It is a set of separate programmes. Each has its own call (convocatoria) published in the BOE and the national grants database (BDNS), and each call names the eligible countries.

We checked every MAEC-AECID call in the grants database for the last three cycles. Pakistan is not named in any of them:
2026-27 África-Med Máster: African and Middle Eastern countries only.
2026-27 Escuela Diplomática: Latin America, Africa and the Middle East, the Philippines and Ukraine. The Philippines is the only Asian country.
2025-26 Programa Máster: 11 Latin American countries and the Philippines.
2024-25 combined call: Latin America, Africa, the Middle East and the Philippines.
The other programmes (Colegio de Europa, Real Academia de España en Roma, Lectorados) are for Spanish citizens, not foreign students.

Tell the student this plainly at the first meeting.

sections.title: Important dates
sections.body:
There is no single annual date. Each programme has its own call, and the window is only 10 working days from the day after the BOE extract is published.

Last cycle (2026-27), for reference:
Escuela Diplomática: BOE extract 20 May 2026, applications until 3 June 2026.
África-Med Máster: BOE extract 1 July 2026, applications 2 to 15 July 2026.
Previous Programa Máster (2025-26, Latin America and Philippines): resolution of 14 February 2025.

The 2027-28 calls have not been published. The timing has moved between cycles (December, February, May and July have all been used), so no date can be given for the next call.

sections.title: Who can apply (in the programmes that exist)
sections.body:
The 2026-27 master's calls required all of the following:
1. Citizenship of a country named in the call.
2. Permanent (not temporary) civil servant or public employee in the home country, including public school and university staff.
3. Written permission from a line manager to study abroad.
4. Admission to an official, in-person master's in Spain of up to 60 ECTS (África-Med required the admission before applying).
5. Knowledge of Spanish. The call does not set a level. NOTE — verify whether a DELE certificate or a specific level is expected in the next call.
6. No Spanish NIE, no EU dual nationality, never resident in the EU, and no earlier AECID award since 2015-16.

This is a scholarship for serving public officials, not for fresh graduates.

sections.title: What it pays
sections.body:
2026-27 África-Med Máster: EUR 2,000 per month plus health insurance in Spain, 1 September 2026 to 31 July 2027. Up to 30 awards.
2026-27 Escuela Diplomática: EUR 1,500 per month plus health insurance in Spain, 1 October 2026 to 30 June 2027. Up to 11 awards.

The call extracts list only the monthly allowance and health insurance. NOTE — verify in the full call whether tuition or travel is covered before quoting either.
Neither call is open to Pakistani citizens.

sections.title: How to apply (if a future call names Pakistan)
sections.body:
1. Find the call in the BOE or the BDNS grants database and check that Pakistan is named in the country list.
2. Get admission to an eligible official master's in Spain (for Escuela Diplomática, apply for admission by the route the call gives).
3. Register in the Carpeta del Ciudadano on the AECID e-office (sede electrónica), preferably with the passport.
4. Fill in the online form entirely in Spanish and upload every document as a PDF.
5. Submit within the 10 working days. Only online applications count.
6. Watch the e-office for the provisional list of admitted and excluded applicants. There are 10 days to fix a defect.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.body:
Valid passport.
Degree and transcripts, HEC-attested. NOTE — verify what further legalisation (MOFA, Spanish Embassy in Islamabad) the Spanish university asks for.
Proof of permanent public employment (the contract cannot be temporary).
Line manager's permission to study abroad for the year.
Master's admission letter, or proof of the admission application.
Proof of Spanish.
Documents not in Spanish need a translation into Spanish; the call says it does not have to be official. Every file must be a PDF.

sections.title: What actually funds a Pakistani student in Spain
sections.body:
Realistic routes, in this order:
1. Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters. English-taught, open to Pakistani citizens, and many consortia include Spanish universities. Listed separately on this tab.
2. The university's own scholarship or fee reduction. NOTE — verify the fee for the specific programme; public master's fees for non-EU students are set by each region and vary widely.
3. Regional government or university grants, usually Spanish-taught.

Spain has no large national government scholarship that is reliably open to Pakistani students. Say so early.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Reading "América Latina, África y Asia" in a call title and assuming Pakistan is included. The only Asian country named in recent calls is the Philippines.
Trusting scholarship blogs that describe MAEC-AECID as open to all countries.
Missing that it is only for permanent public employees.
Waiting for a fixed date: the window is 10 working days and is announced only in the BOE.

name: OeAD Ernst Mach Grant — Worldwide
region: National — OeAD, Austria's Agency for Education and Internationalisation
call_notes: Research grant only: not for a master's degree or a full PhD in Austria. The 2027/28 call is open now until 1 December 2026, and results are expected in early July 2027.
benefits: Help arranging accommodation and health insurance. Does not cover all costs; own funds are expected.

sections.title: Not for master's students
sections.body:
Read this before offering it. OeAD states the grant is "not intended to finance a complete or parts of a regular PhD, Master or study programme in Austria."

It funds a research stay of 1 to 9 months in Austria for:
PhD students enrolled at a university outside Austria.
Recent graduates and postdocs who want to research in Austria.
Postdocs working as lecturers or researchers at a university outside Austria.

A student looking for funding for a taught master's in Austria is not eligible. Look at university scholarships and other programmes on grants.at instead.

sections.title: Important dates
sections.body:
Applications for 2027/28: September 2026 to 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET.
Results: expected early July 2027.
Earliest arrival: September 2027. Stays fall within the academic year 2027/28.

The deadline moved. The 2026/27 round closed on 1 February 2026; the 2027/28 round closes on 1 December 2026. Do not rely on the older date.

The Austrian supervisor may set an earlier internal deadline. WU Vienna's tax law institute, for example, asks for requests by 1 November 2026.

sections.title: Who can apply
sections.body:
Young researchers from all disciplines and all countries except Austria.

Graduates must have finished their studies at a university outside Austria after 30 September 2025.

Age: not older than 35 when the research stay starts.

A written confirmation of supervision from a lecturer at an Austrian university, on the OeAD template, dated, signed and stamped, and no older than six months.

English good enough for the subject area. No official test certificate is required.

sections.title: What it pays
sections.body:
€1,300 per month for 1 to 9 months. No extensions.
NOTE — verify: the OeAD pages do not state the rate; €1,300 comes from the grants.at listing as quoted by WU Vienna and other sources.

OeAD helps arrange accommodation and health insurance.

OeAD says the grant may not cover all costs, and own funds are expected. The applicant pays for compulsory health insurance, travel to Austria and travel to the Austrian embassy. If rent is above €386.43 per month (2026 figure), extra proof of funds may be needed for the residence permit.

sections.title: How to apply
sections.body:
1. Confirm the candidate fits: PhD student, recent graduate (after 30 September 2025) or postdoc, 35 or younger at the start.
2. Find an Austrian university lecturer willing to supervise the project.
3. Get the supervision confirmation on the OeAD template, signed and stamped.
4. Agree the stay dates (whole months, 1 to 9, from September 2027).
5. Create an account on grants.at and complete the online application for Ernst Mach Grant Worldwide.
6. Submit by 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET.
7. Wait for results in early July 2027, then start the visa or residence permit at once.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.body:
Supervision confirmation from the Austrian lecturer (OeAD template).
CV including date of birth.
Publication list.
Research proposal, or a summary of the doctoral thesis.
Planned stay dates.
Degree certificates and transcripts.
NOTE — verify the full list in the grants.at application form; this list follows the OeAD FAQ and WU Vienna's supervisor request.

sections.title: For Pakistani students
sections.body:
Suitable for Pakistani PhD scholars and early-career faculty, for example HEC-funded PhD students who want a research stay, not for master's applicants.

ASEA-UNINET: the Ernst Mach ASEA-UNINET grant is only for citizens of Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam. It is not a route for Pakistanis.

HEC attestation: NOTE — verify whether OeAD or the Austrian mission asks for attested degrees; attest early.

Visa: results come in July and stays start from September, so the time is short. A Pakistani grantee will need an Austrian visa or residence permit through the Austrian Embassy Islamabad. NOTE — verify the permit type for the length of stay and current processing times with the embassy.

sections.title: Other Ernst Mach variants
sections.body:
Ernst Mach Grant for Fachhochschule: for undergraduates and graduates from non-European universities, 4 to 10 months at an Austrian university of applied sciences, age 35 or under, applications October to 1 February. NOTE — verify whether it funds study or only research or project work, and the rate, before offering it.

Ernst Mach Follow-Up Grant: postdocs and lecturers from non-European developing countries, 1 to 3 months, age 45 or under, deadline 1 February. NOTE — verify whether it is limited to former Ernst Mach grantees.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Offering it to a student who wants a funded master's degree.
Applying without a signed and stamped Austrian supervision letter, or with one older than six months.
Using the old 1 February date; the 2027/28 deadline is 1 December 2026.
Applying when the degree was finished before 30 September 2025, or when the applicant will be over 35 at the start.
Assuming the grant covers all costs.
Sending a Pakistani applicant down the ASEA-UNINET route.

name: Guillaume Dupaix International Master's Scholarship (University of Luxembourg)
region: University of Luxembourg (talent support programme funded by Luxembourg ministries)
application_deadline: Expected late March 2027, together with the master's application (last round: 24 March 2026). NOTE — verify when the 2027/2028 dates are published.
call_notes: The University says applications for 2027-2028 open on 1 February 2027. The scholarship is applied for through the master's application, only on invitation; the last round's deadline was 24 March 2026.
stipend_amount: €5,763 per semester (€11,526 a year), up to 2 years
benefits: Part living costs, part accommodation, plus priority for a university residence room if requested early. No tuition or registration fee waiver.

sections.title: Important dates
sections.body:
Last completed round (2026/2027 entry):
Master's application and scholarship application: by 24 March 2026
Missing scholarship documents: by 31 March 2026
Outcome: 15 May 2026 (selected and waiting-list applicants informed by email)
Acceptance: within 3 working days of the offer
Waiting list and agreement signature: through autumn 2026 (agreements signed no sooner than October)

Next round (2027/2028 entry): the University says applications open on 1 February 2027. It has a single September intake.
Expect the scholarship deadline in late March 2027. NOTE — verify, as the University says its 2027-2028 criteria are under review.

sections.title: Who can apply
sections.body:
Full-time applicants to a University of Luxembourg master's programme, in any field. It is open to EU/EEA and non-EU students alike, so Pakistani students are eligible.

Not eligible:
Programmes with an outgoing mobility semester or year abroad.
Applicants for or holders of Luxembourg State Financial Aid for Higher Education (MengStudien, formerly AideFi).

Places: 30 a year (10 per faculty). 15 are open to students from any country; 15 are reserved for target countries (Western Balkans, Ibero-American countries, Thailand, Vietnam, Belarus, Egypt, India, Moldova, Russia, United Kingdom, Turkey, Ukraine).
Pakistan is not a target country, so a Pakistani student competes for the 15 open places.

sections.title: What it pays
sections.body:
€5,763 per semester, which is €11,526 a year.
Paid for up to 2 years, the standard length of a master's.
It covers part of living costs and accommodation. It does not cover tuition, and no fee waiver is possible.

Recipients get priority for a room in a University residence, provided they apply for accommodation early (the University emails them). Waiting-list recipients selected later in the year lose that priority.

Luxembourg is expensive. The award will not cover everything, and the student still needs to show funds for the residence permit. NOTE — verify the current proof-of-funds amount with the Luxembourg Immigration Directorate.

sections.title: How to apply
sections.body:
1. Choose up to three master's programmes on uni.lu (an application cannot be changed or deleted once created). Avoid programmes with a compulsory semester abroad.
2. Check the admission and language criteria (CEFR level for every teaching language) on each programme page.
3. From 1 February 2027, create an account on the admissions portal, upload documents and pay the €100 non-refundable application fee per programme. Then click Send your file; paying does not submit it.
4. Submit before the scholarship deadline (24 March in the last round), even if the programme's own deadline is later.
5. Programme directors assess excellence. The strongest applicants receive an email invitation to apply for the scholarship. There is no other way to apply, and email applications are not accepted.
6. Complete the scholarship application and any missing documents by the deadline in the invitation.
7. Results by mid-May. Accept within 3 working days.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.body:
Identity photo and passport copy.
Bachelor's degree certificate and full transcript.
Language certificate for each teaching language at the CEFR level the programme asks for (for English, usually IELTS or TOEFL).
Motivation letter, detailed CV, referee contacts or recommendation letters, where the programme asks.
Official translation of any document not in English, French or German.
After admission (non-EU): recognition of the bachelor's degree by the Luxembourg Ministry of Research and Higher Education, and a criminal record extract for the immigration file.
NOTE — verify the scholarship's own document list; it is only given in the invitation email.

sections.title: For Pakistani students
sections.body:
Get the bachelor's degree and transcript HEC-attested before February. The Luxembourg ministry's degree recognition is required after admission, and a clean attested set speeds it up.
Request the police character certificate (criminal record extract) early. The University advises no later than the beginning of April, even before the admission decision.

English-taught programmes need proof at the CEFR level listed; IELTS is the usual route. Some programmes are bilingual or trilingual and need French or German too.

Visa: non-EU students go through the Luxembourg Ministry of Home Affairs (Immigration Directorate) before the long-stay D visa. NOTE — verify the current steps, which mission handles Luxembourg visas for Pakistan, and processing times. Results arrive mid-May, so start immediately.

The University states it does not work with student recruitment agencies. The student must create and submit the application personally.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Waiting for a separate scholarship call. There is none; the scholarship follows the master's application.
Submitting the master's application after the scholarship deadline because the programme deadline is later.
Choosing a programme with a compulsory semester or year abroad, which is ineligible.
Also applying for MengStudien state aid. The two cannot be combined.
Telling the student tuition is covered. It is not.
Assuming Pakistan is a target country. It is not; the student competes for the 15 open places.
Missing the 3-working-day acceptance window in May.
Leaving the criminal record extract and degree recognition until after admission.

name: Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals (SISGP)
application_deadline: University application by 15 January 2027 (confirmed); SI scholarship window expected in February 2027 (not yet announced)
call_notes: Pakistan is NOT on the 2026/2027 eligible-country list (34 countries). Check the new list when SI publishes the 2027/2028 documents, expected mid-November 2026, before advising anyone.
stipend_amount: SEK 12,000/month, plus a one-off SEK 15,000 travel grant
benefits: Full tuition paid directly to the university, monthly living allowance, travel grant, and membership of the SI Network for Global Professionals. No insurance.

sections.title: Pakistan is not eligible this round
sections.body:
The 2026/2027 call on si.se lists 34 eligible countries. Pakistan is not one of them.
Bangladesh is the only South Asian country on the list.
The 2026 recipients list (189 awards) has no Pakistani scholars.

Some blogs and older guides still show Pakistan. They are out of date.

The list is set each round. Check it again when SI publishes the 2027/2028 documents (expected mid-November 2026). Until then, do not tell a Pakistani student they can apply.

A student who also holds citizenship of an eligible country may apply on that citizenship. Only one application is allowed; using two citizenships disqualifies every application.

sections.title: Important dates
sections.body:
Last completed round (2026/2027):
16 October 2025 to 15 January 2026: university applications on universityadmissions.se.
Mid-November 2025: SI published the call documents and eligible programmes.
9 to 25 February 2026: SI portal open, closing 14:59 CET on the last day.
26 March 2026: university admission results.
23 April 2026: scholarship results.

Next round (2027/2028), confirmed by University Admissions:
16 October 2026: application round opens.
15 January 2027: application deadline.
1 February 2027: deadline for the SEK 900 fee and supporting documents.
1 April 2027: master's admission results.

SI's own 2027 dates are not announced. Expect the same pattern: documents in mid-November, a two-week portal in February.

sections.title: Two deadlines, and the first one is not the scholarship
sections.body:
1. Apply for up to four master's programmes on universityadmissions.se by 15 January. Pay the fee and upload documents by 1 February.
2. Then apply to SI in the February window, quoting the eight-digit University Admissions application number.

The student must be admitted or conditionally admitted to an eligible programme on the first results day. Reserve places and late admissions do not count, and changing or declining the offer removes the student from the running.
A student who hears about SISGP in February has already missed it.

sections.title: Who can apply
sections.body:
1. Citizen of an eligible country (no need to live there).
2. Liable to pay tuition fees in Sweden.
3. Applied to eligible English-taught master's programmes (list published each November).
4. Work experience: at least 3,000 hours before the February of the application year, from no more than three employers. Full-time or part-time, as employee, freelancer or employer. Applicants from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine have no minimum.
5. Leadership experience from a job or from civil society. No minimum hours, but leadership from employment is preferred.

Work and leadership are evidenced on SI's own form, signed and stamped by the employer or a notary.
Not eligible: anyone enrolled at or holding a degree from a Swedish university, anyone who has lived in Sweden two years or more, or a previous SI scholarship holder.

sections.title: What it pays
sections.body:
Full tuition, paid by SI to the university each semester.
SEK 12,000 per month for living costs, for the whole study period.
SEK 15,000 one-off travel grant (SEK 10,000 for six Eastern Partnership countries).
Membership of the SI Network for Global Professionals.

It does not cover insurance, family members, the SEK 900 application fee, a change of programme or an extension.

sections.title: Documents SI asks for
sections.body:
All in English, on SI's templates for that year:
1. CV on the SI template, three pages at most.
2. Proof of work and leadership experience on the SI form: typed, printed, signed by the referee, stamped by the organisation or a notary, uploaded as one PDF.
3. Two reference letters on the SI form from two different referees; one must be about work. Signed, stamped, one PDF.
4. Copy of a valid passport or national ID.
5. A motivation written in the portal. Some applicants are randomly asked for a short video.

A wrong form, a missing stamp or a missing document means disqualification without assessment.

sections.title: For Pakistani students (universityadmissions.se)
sections.body:
This applies to any Pakistani applying to Sweden, with or without SISGP.

Entry: a 4-year bachelor's (minimum 124 credits), or a bachelor's plus a master's. If the university was HEC category Z or Y and the degree was issued before 1 January 2012, 5 years of study are needed.
Attestation: every transcript and degree must be attested by HEC, including transcripts of unfinished studies. Both parts of a two-part Detailed Marks Certificate are needed.
HEC attestations from before February 2009 (stamp number under 200,000) must be redone.
The HEC stamp digits must be readable on the scan and not covered by other stamps.
College-issued mark sheets count only if countersigned by the university's Controller of Examinations and HEC-attested.
Documents are uploaded as scans to universityadmissions.se. No translation is needed.
Name and date of birth must match on every document and the account. An affidavit is not accepted to explain a difference.
English: Pakistani school English does not count. Use an approved test such as IELTS. NOTE — verify the score for the programme; most master's ask for English 6.
Application fee: SEK 900, once per semester, not refundable, due by 1 February 2027.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Believing a blog that says Pakistan is eligible.
Applying to SI without a university application made by 15 January.
Not paying the SEK 900 by 1 February, so the university application is never assessed.
Being only a reserve on results day.
Claiming hours toward the 3,000 without employer proof on the SI form.
Using last year's templates, or leaving off the stamp.
Waiting until the last day: the portal slows down and closes at 14:59 CET.

sections.body:

name: Finnish University Tuition-Fee Waivers
application_deadline: No national Finland Scholarship since 2024. University fee waivers are applied for inside the admission form: Aalto 5 Jan 2027, Tampere 7 Jan 2027, Helsinki 19 Jan 2027, national joint application 21 Jan 2027 (all 15:00 Finnish time).
call_notes: The Ministry-funded Finland Scholarship (100% waiver plus €5,000) ran 2022–2024 and is not granted in current admissions. What remains is each university's own tuition fee waiver, applied for with the master's application; the first 2027 window (Aalto) opens 7 Dec 2026.
stipend_amount: None now — university tuition fee waivers only (50% or 100%); no living allowance
benefits: Partial or full tuition fee waiver from the admitting university, continued in year two only with full-time progress (Helsinki: at least 55 ECTS a year).

sections.title: The Finland Scholarship has ended
sections.body:
The national Finland Scholarship, funded by the Ministry of Education and Culture, ran from 2022 to 2024.
It gave a 100% tuition fee waiver plus a one-off €5,000 relocation grant.
Aalto University states it "will not be granted in future admissions".

Study in Finland now says plainly: there are no governmental scholarship programmes for bachelor's or master's studies.
Do not promise a student the €5,000 grant.
Many Pakistani websites and agents still advertise a "fully funded Finland government scholarship" — Study in Finland calls these posts misleading.

sections.title: Important dates
sections.body:
Master's programmes starting autumn 2027 (all on Studyinfo.fi, 15:00 Finnish time):
Aalto University: 7 Dec 2026 to 5 Jan 2027. Documents by 12 Jan 2027. Results from 30 Mar 2027.
Tampere University: 14 Dec 2026 to 7 Jan 2027.
University of Helsinki: 5 to 19 Jan 2027.
National joint application (most other universities and UAS): 7 to 21 Jan 2027.

Last round, for autumn 2026:
Helsinki: 2 to 16 Jan 2026, results by 15 Apr 2026.
Joint application: 7 to 21 Jan 2026, all results by 27 May 2026.

The fee waiver deadline is the admission deadline. It cannot be applied for after the window closes (Aalto).

sections.title: Who can apply
sections.body:
Citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who must pay tuition fees, applying to an English-taught bachelor's or master's programme.
Pakistani citizens qualify.

Waivers are merit-based and very competitive; only the strongest applicants in each programme get one.
They cover tuition only. The student must fund all living costs.
At some universities a waiver is decided at admission; at others it is awarded later, after studies begin.

sections.title: What it pays
sections.body:
Tuition fee waivers only. No stipend, no travel, no relocation grant.

University of Helsinki: 50% or 100% waiver. Most awards are 50%. Fees 13,000 to 18,000 euros a year.
Aalto University: Excellence Scholarship covers the full fee. Master's fees from 1 Aug 2025: 15,000 (business), 17,000 (technology), 20,000 (arts and architecture) euros a year.
Tampere University: 50% of the fee for the programme duration, for a limited number. Master's fee 12,000 euros a year. Everyone else gets a 2,000 euro early bird reduction in year one.

Year two is conditional. Helsinki requires full-time study, at least 55 ECTS a year, and checks progress after year one. Aalto requires full-time study to the approved study plan.

sections.title: How to apply
sections.body:
1. Shortlist programmes on Studyinfo.fi and each university's site. Note each university's own window.
2. Check the programme's English requirement and country-specific document rules for Pakistan.
3. Get the bachelor's degree and transcript attested by HEC (see below).
4. Submit the application on Studyinfo.fi and pay the 100 euro application fee (one fee per intake term for non-EU applicants).
5. On the same form, answer "yes" to the scholarship / fee waiver question. There is no separate scholarship form.
6. Upload all documents by the university's attachment deadline.
7. Accept the study place, pay the remaining fee, and apply for the residence permit straight away.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.body:
Passport.
Bachelor's degree certificate and full transcript, HEC-attested on every page.
English test result (IELTS Academic or another accepted test). NOTE — verify the minimum score on each programme page; the university pages checked do not give one general figure.
CV and motivation letter; some programmes also ask for a preliminary assignment or references.
For the residence permit: admission letter, fee payment receipt or waiver certificate, bank statement, health insurance.

sections.title: For Pakistani students
sections.body:
HEC attestation: University Admissions Finland requires the degree certificate and transcript to be attested by HEC, with every page stamped and signed. Attestations from before 20 September 2009 are rejected and must be redone.
Degrees from affiliated colleges are not accepted. The degree and transcript must be issued by the main university or a college with degree-awarding status.
The HEC stamp numbers must be readable on the scan.

Residence permit (Migri, applied online in Enter Finland):
Proof of funds: at least 800 euros a month, i.e. 9,600 euros in the student's bank account when applying, for a programme of a year or more.
If the fee is not yet paid, the account must also hold the first year's fee. Living-cost money cannot be counted towards the fee.
A 50% waiver still leaves half the fee to show.
The student must visit a Finnish mission in person to prove identity and give fingerprints. NOTE — verify whether this is done at the Embassy in Islamabad or a service centre in Karachi/Lahore.
Processing can take several months. Apply the day the study place is accepted.
NOTE — verify on migri.fi: students may work on average 30 hours a week.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Telling a student about the €5,000 grant or "Finland government scholarship". It ended in 2024.
Ticking "no" or leaving the scholarship question blank. It cannot be added later.
Missing Aalto and Tampere because they close before the joint application.
Applying with affiliated-college documents or old (pre-2009) HEC attestation.
Assuming a 100% waiver: at Helsinki most awards are 50%.
Showing the fee money and living money as the same funds to Migri.
Not telling the student that year two depends on earning at least 55 ECTS.

name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM)
application_deadline: Set by each consortium, mostly October 2026 to January 2027 for a September 2027 start. Some close earlier (MARIHE closed 21 Sep 2026).
call_notes: There is no central round: each joint master opens and closes on its own date, and a few 2027 intakes have already closed. Build each student's shortlist from the EACEA catalogue now and record every programme's own deadline.
stipend_amount: €1,400 a month for the full programme (12, 18 or 24 months)
benefits: No tuition or other mandatory fees for scholarship holders, insurance, and €1,400 a month towards travel, visa, installation and living costs.

sections.title: Shown for every European destination
sections.body:
An Erasmus Mundus joint masters is run by a consortium of at least three universities in three countries, so it is not tied to one destination.
This entry appears on the Scholarship tab for every European country the office sends students to. There is only one copy to keep up to date.

sections.title: Important dates
sections.body:
No central deadline. Each consortium sets its own.
The EU says most programmes take applications between October and January for the following academic year.
For a September 2027 start, expect most deadlines between October 2026 and January 2027.
Some close much earlier: MARIHE's 2027 intake closed on 21 Sep 2026.
Scholarship deadlines are often earlier than the self-funded deadline on the same programme.

The EACEA catalogue currently lists 218 programmes. Newly selected programmes publish their dates in autumn.
NOTE — verify each programme's deadline on its own website; do not rely on list sites.

sections.title: Who can apply
sections.body:
Students from any country, including Pakistan.
A first degree (bachelor's or recognised equivalent), or final-year students who will graduate before the programme starts.
Students who have already held an EMJM scholarship cannot get a second one.
The scholarship is for full-time students only.
Each consortium sets its own academic, English and subject requirements and selects its own scholarship holders.

sections.title: What it pays
sections.body:
Scholarship: 1,400 euros a month, for the whole programme (12, 18 or 24 months). This is the unit cost in the Erasmus+ Programme Guide 2026.
It is meant to cover travel, visa, installation and living costs; the consortium pays it, not Brussels.
A 24-month programme is 33,600 euros in total.

Consortia may not charge scholarship holders tuition fees or other mandatory participation costs, and may not charge application fees.
Full insurance cover for enrolled students is paid from the programme's institutional budget.
NOTE — verify with the consortium how and when the monthly payments are made; it differs by programme.

sections.title: How to apply
sections.body:
1. Search the EACEA catalogue by field and country. Check the programme says it still offers EMJM scholarships; some do not.
2. Open each programme's own website and note its scholarship deadline, requirements and mobility track.
3. Prepare HEC-attested documents, English test and references early; references often have to be uploaded by the deadline too.
4. Apply on the consortium's own portal and tick that you are applying for the Erasmus Mundus scholarship.
5. Apply to several programmes; each is a separate application with its own date.
6. After an offer, sign the Student Agreement and start the visa for the first country at once.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.body:
Passport.
Bachelor's degree and transcripts (final-year students: latest transcript), HEC-attested, with certified English translations where needed.
English test: IELTS Academic or TOEFL as the programme specifies. NOTE — verify the score on each programme page; 6.5 overall is common but not universal.
Motivation letter written for that programme.
CV (many programmes ask for Europass format).
Two recommendation letters, often submitted directly by the referees.
Proof of residence (passport or residence certificate), used to apply the residence rules.

sections.title: For Pakistani students
sections.body:
Pakistan is a "third country not associated to the Programme" (Region 5, Asia). The old term was "Partner country".
Since 2021 the scholarship amount is the same for every nationality. The old Partner-country and Programme-country scholarship categories, and the rule counting anyone who had lived more than 12 months in Europe as a Programme-country candidate, belong to the 2014–2020 programme and are not in the current Programme Guide.
NOTE — verify on each consortium's page: some programmes still publish their own residence conditions.

What does apply now:
The two compulsory study periods must be in two countries other than the student's country of residence at enrolment.
No more than 10% of a programme's scholarships may go to one nationality, so Pakistani applicants compete with each other for a small share.
Consortia may receive extra top-up scholarships for Asia (Region 5) under the EU's external budget, which Pakistani students can benefit from.

Get the degree and transcript HEC-attested before applying. NOTE — verify on each programme page whether attested or certified copies are required at application or only at enrolment. A separate student visa is needed for each country of study; the consortium usually issues letters for this.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Treating it as one scholarship with one deadline.
Missing the scholarship deadline because the self-funded deadline is later.
Applying to a programme that no longer offers scholarships.
A generic motivation letter sent to every programme.
Late reference letters or English results.
Planning a mobility track in the student's own country of residence.
Telling a student the old Partner-country 12-month rule decides eligibility.

sections.title: Why it is worth the effort
sections.body:
It funds a Pakistani student across several European countries on one award, with fees waived and a monthly allowance.
There is no general work-experience requirement of the kind SISGP and DAAD EPOS impose, so it suits a strong student straight out of a bachelor's.

sections.title: Useful links / contact
sections.body:
Erasmus+ EMJM page for students: https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/opportunities/opportunities-for-individuals/students/erasmus-mundus-joint-masters
EACEA catalogue of programmes: https://www.eacea.ec.europa.eu/scholarships/erasmus-mundus-catalogue_en
Erasmus+ Programme Guide 2026 (EMJM rules, amounts): https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2025-11/programme-guide-2026_en.pdf
Example consortium (MARIHE): https://www.marihe.eu/
Questions about a programme go to that consortium's own contact address, not to EACEA.
